findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The deleteCacheMutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop on success, whereas the disconnectMutation right below it explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations` in its `onSettled` callback. If the parent component does not pass an `onChanged`/`onSuccess` handler that performs the same invalidation, the dropdown will keep showing the stale 'Cache Status'/'Last updated' timestamp after the cache has actually been deleted, because the `connectedCalendars` query (which supplies `cacheUpdatedAt`) is never refetched.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {...}).format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt))` hardcodes the locale to en-US instead of using the user's active locale (available via `useLocale()`/`i18n.language`). In a multi-locale product like cal.com, this means the cache-updated timestamp will always render in US date/time format regardless of the user's configured language/region settings.

findings.title: Cache deletion bypasses CalendarCacheRepository abstraction
findings.body: deleteCacheHandler calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly instead of going through `CalendarCacheRepository`/`CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` (which already exposes a `deleteManyByCredential` method used elsewhere in the codebase to gate behavior behind the calendar-cache feature flag). Bypassing the repository abstraction is inconsistent with the rest of the calendar-cache feature and could allow cache deletion even when calendar caching is supposed to be disabled for a tenant via the mock repository.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId updates all SelectedCalendars, not just the ones refreshed
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after processing only the `selectedCalendars` passed into the function. However `updateManyByCredentialId` updates every SelectedCalendar row for that credentialId, including rows that were not part of the batch being refreshed (e.g. in `unwatchCalendar`, `remainingCalendars` excludes the calendar being unwatched, yet its `updatedAt` would still be bumped by this call). This makes the 'last updated' timestamp inaccurate for calendars whose availability was not actually re-fetched in this call.

findings.title: dev:cron now relies on npx tsx without adding tsx as a dependency
findings.body: The `dev:cron` script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not added to `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` remains, still used by other scripts). This forces `npx` to resolve/download `tsx` on every invocation (network dependency, non-pinned version), which can fail in offline/CI environments and introduces inconsistent tooling between scripts.

findings.title: sed -i '' syntax is BSD-only and breaks on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS sed syntax for in-place editing (`-i ''`). On GNU/Linux sed (common in CI and most dev containers), this will either error out or incorrectly treat `''` as the script, breaking the script for non-macOS contributors.

findings.title: No tests added for the destructive deleteCache feature
findings.body: This PR introduces a new destructive mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`), a new UI component (`CredentialActionsDropdown`) with confirmation dialogs, and a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), but no unit or integration tests were added for any of them. Given that deleteCache permanently removes cached calendar availability data and the PR's own review checklist flags end-to-end verification as still outstanding, lack of automated test coverage for authorization (credential ownership check) and the delete logic itself is a notable gap.
